title: External import over REST answers a tenancy-service outage as 400 instead of 503
body:
domain:server#6 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CXCS98uhsFQYk64epE

Found by the contract review of PR #30602 (#30469 item 2), record on that PR at head `100d47a7`, ④ should-fix.

## What

From PR #30602 on, the external-datasource import reads the effective tenancy posture (`classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture`) to decide where an imported object lands. That read throws `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` (`status 503`, `code SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`) when a registered `tenancy` service cannot answer (the #16013 rule in `packages/core/src/security/admission-tenancy-posture.ts`).

`packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes.ts` `answerThrown` relays only sandbox faults and `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`; everything else becomes `400 EXTERNAL_IMPORT_ERROR`. So `POST /api/v1/datasources/:name/external/tables/:remote/import` tells the caller the request was malformed when the truth is "the service is unavailable, retry". Nothing is saved, so it is not permissive.

The twins already get it right: `packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts` `badRequest` relays the `503` / `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` envelope, and the MCP `import_object` tool relays it (`thrownRefusalEnvelope` reads `status` and `code`).

## Expected

`answerThrown` relays an error carrying `status 503` and `code SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` as that envelope, the way `badRequest` does, with a pin: a `tenancy` service whose posture read throws makes the REST import answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and saves nothing.

## Surface

`packages/rest/src/external-datasource-routes.ts` and its test; a `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/rest`. Not BREAKING (an error status corrected from 400 to 503 for an outage).
